extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners on requesting, conducting, and documenting interviews with applicants/representatives during patent prosecution to clarify issues, discuss prior art, and advance prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are an effective examination tool and are an opportunity to explain rejections, discuss prior art, clarify positions, and resolve issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews can be useful at any stage of prosecution; they can lead to a better understanding of Applicant’s invention, bridge the knowledge gap between Examiner and Applicant, help reach agreement and advance prosecution, and promote compact prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough preparation is required prior to an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for an agenda (PTOL-413A) to outline purpose and intent; thoroughly review the record including the prior art; focus on the issues identified and look for opportunities to resolve them; consult with your SPE or Primary Examiner and discuss the relevant issues before the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should approach interviews cooperatively and with an open mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be receptive to different interpretations of claim language and prior art during the interview; actively listen and try to understand Applicant’s position before drawing conclusions; keep in mind the applicant’s position and look for areas of agreement; remember the common goal is to advance prosecution and be willing to resolve issues and cooperate with Applicant to achieve this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews require clear, professional, and attentive communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the Office’s position; use appropriate tone and volume of voice; watch body language and make eye contact; be polite, respectful, and always act in a professional manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization of interview requestor
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the person requesting the interview is authorized to prosecute the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requestor must be a registered practitioner and Attorney of Record (see MPEP 713.05). Examiners should ensure the requestor is authorized before granting the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview request procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps to take when receiving an interview request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquire about the purpose or intent of the interview; request an agenda (PTOL-413A) to identify specific issues for discussion so both parties can prepare; discuss the case with your SPE or Primary Examiner and, depending on signatory and negotiation authority, ask them to attend; follow-up promptly with the attorney (and your SPE/Primary Examiner if applicable) to schedule a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible interview topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Common substantive topics appropriate for interview discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature of the invention and state of the art (what problem was solved/what improvement is provided); claim interpretation and scope (e.g., preamble, functional language, means-plus-function, intended use language, non-positive claim language, clarity); meaning of particular limitations and how supported by the specification; broadest reasonable interpretation of the claim; statutory subject matter; prior art; rejections and objections; proposed amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested sequence for an effective interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended step-by-step flow for conducting an interview to maximize effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Prior to interview, prepare by reviewing the record and agenda, and discuss with SPE/Primary Examiner if applicable. 2) At the interview, give the applicant an opportunity to explain the invention and novel features and discuss agenda issues. 3) Openly discuss how inventive concepts are relayed or not relayed in the claims. 4) Discuss prior art and rejections. 5) Seek to establish common ground and understanding. 6) Follow up with applicant on any unresolved issues. 7) Document the results of the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting interviews — accessibility and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for granting interview requests and accommodating interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no bad time for an interview if it can help further prosecution, shorten pendency, or provide a benefit to the Examiner. Be accessible (answer phone, promptly return voicemail), be flexible in scheduling and seek mutually agreed times and venues, consider telephonic interviews if in-person cannot be scheduled, do not deny an in-person request without seeking a mutually agreeable time to hold a telephone interview, telephonic interviews can be conducted from an alternate work site; examiners on hoteling or flexible schedules must be available during regular working hours and may need schedule adjustments to accommodate interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denying interview requests — typical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which an interview would not normally be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview requests may be denied when: an appeal brief has already been filed in the application; the requestor is not a registered attorney; the interview is not prearranged (e.g., attorney/applicant shows up without prior notice). Despite these exceptions, examiners are expected and encouraged to grant interviews where appropriate to resolve or clarify issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling interview requests from persons not of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure when the interview requestor is not listed as counsel of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if the individual is the inventor or a registered practitioner. If the inventor has legal representation, notify them that their attorney must schedule the interview. If a pro se inventor, grant the interview under normal procedures. If an unregistered practitioner, deny the interview (see MPEP 713.05). If a registered practitioner, have them supply a power of attorney before the interview; if a power of attorney cannot be supplied, the interview is conducted solely from the practitioner’s file — the Examiner’s and USPTO’s files are closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting an interview (use PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for documenting interviews and what must be included in the Interview Summary form (PTOL-413).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Examiner’s Interview Summary form (PTOL-413). An interview summary should include attendees and date; prior art, claims and exhibits discussed; details of the discussion (specifics about issues discussed, claim limitations, any proposed claim amendments, and any agreement as to allowability of claims or next steps). Document agreements reached or not reached (e.g., allowability, interpretation of claim language, priority dates, application of case law, next steps such as filing a proposed amendment or withdrawing a rejection). If a proposed amendment is agreed to, attach a copy or otherwise make the record clear as to what was agreed to. If electronic communication (e-mail) has been authorized by applicant, attach copies of all e-mail correspondence. Do not include comments of a personal nature. Any discussion that touches on merits of the invention or application is to be considered an interview and should be documented. The purpose of the interview summary is to complete and clarify the record; do not prosecute “off the record.” Further guidance in MPEP 713.04, 502.01, 502.02, and 502.03.
